name: Liquid democracy
summary: Liquid democracy is a hybrid of direct and representative democracy in which every voter may vote on each issue personally or delegate that vote to someone they trust, by topic or across the board. Delegations can be passed on and taken back at any time, so representatives hold power only while they keep voters' confidence. It is a procedural idea, usually put into practice through online platforms, and takes no side on most economic or social questions.
scope: The mainstream strand as developed since the 2000s in Berlin hacker and Pirate-party circles and the LiquidFeedback software (Behrens, Kistner, Nitsche, Swierczek), plus scholarly accounts such as Valsangiacomo's. It treats liquid democracy as a complement to representative institutions, not a revolutionary program. Because it is a decision procedure, most substantive policy statements are answered neutral with low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Liquid democracy is a decision procedure; its sources say nothing on health policy, and Pirate-party and civic users hold varied views, so no stance is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors are a policy outcome the voters would decide through the system; the model itself takes no side.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ideology prescribes how collective decisions are made, not whether markets or governments should allocate resources.

public-ownership.rationale: Whether industries are public is left to what delegated and direct votes decide; adherents range across the spectrum.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax rates are substantive policy the procedure leaves open; no source ties liquid democracy to a tax position.

unions-good.rationale: Nothing in the model concerns labor organization; users come from tech, Pirate and civic circles with mixed views.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights are not part of liquid democracy's doctrine, which concerns voting and delegation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: A procedural model with no stated line on business regulation; the answer depends on the voters who use it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare levels are outcomes of whatever majorities choose, not a commitment of the model.

worker-ownership.rationale: Liquid democracy has been proposed for firms and associations as a voting method, but no source commits it to worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Pirate-party users who built the tools stress transparency and privacy against state surveillance, though the model itself is silent; inferred from that milieu.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is outside the model's concerns; Pirate-party adherents lean liberal but the method itself is neutral.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech regulation is not addressed by the model; adherents are split between free-expression and anti-hate positions.

strong-leader.rationale: The model puts issues rather than leaders at the centre and spreads power through revocable delegations, which is opposed to a leader bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Liquid democracy is a way of running collective decision-making and assumes public institutions exist to be steered by voters; it is not anti-state.

limit-guns.rationale: No source links liquid democracy to a gun policy; it is left to voters.

empower-police-military.rationale: Security funding is substantive policy the procedure does not settle.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A social question outside the model; Pirate-milieu users lean liberal but this is not stated by the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Delegation lets people choose who decides and issue-level voting pushes decisions toward those affected, but the sources do not say decisions should be local; also used at national scale.

rehabilitation.rationale: Criminal justice philosophy is not part of the model.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; a procedural ideology takes no stand on family forms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social policy is outside the model; the voters using it decide.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the model is neutral on moral-social questions.

more-religion-public.rationale: The model is silent on religion's public role, so the answer is left neutral.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: No source connects liquid democracy to remedial racial policy; adherents differ.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A theoretical question about gender the ideology does not address.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural policy is outside the model, which has been used by internationally minded Pirate parties and local councils alike.

gradual-change.rationale: Adherents typically want institutions made more flexible and responsive, and mostly aim to supplement elections rather than overthrow them; slightly against deference to established forms.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration levels are substantive policy the procedure leaves open.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Liquid democracy could in theory be scaled up but no source takes a position on international bodies.

free-trade.rationale: An economic policy question outside the model.

nation-first.rationale: Foreign-policy orientation is not part of the doctrine.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed by sources on liquid democracy.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; the model concerns decision procedure, not who may enter.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental economics is outside the model's scope.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Left to voters; no source ties the model to a climate stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The model's advocates build software to fix representative democracy's flaws, which implies a hopeful view of technology for governance; no general claim is made about all problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is not addressed by the model.

revolution-justified.rationale: LiquidFeedback's authors present it as a complement to existing representative democracy, working within institutions, so revolution is not part of the approach.

experts-over-public.rationale: Topic-specific delegation lets voters hand decisions to experts they choose, but experts have no built-in extra say and each citizen may override; adherents stress both.

central-planning.rationale: An economic-system question the model does not address.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; the model is silent on economic ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: A specific tax policy with no link to the sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is a revenue choice voters would settle; the sources attach no tax stance to liquid democracy.

basic-income.rationale: Some Pirate-party members support it but the model does not, so it is left neutral.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is outside the scope of the model.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic policy is not part of the doctrine.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The distribution of property is a policy outcome outside the model, and its sources never discuss ownership patterns.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in the sources, so no position is inferred and adherents would differ.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Valsangiacomo describes liquid democracy as putting parties and interest groups on a level footing under individual citizen choice, not placing state-recognised bodies at the centre of decisions.

one-party-rule.rationale: The model depends on open competition among delegates, parties and groups, with every voter free to withdraw support, which rules out a single guiding party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary office is at odds with the revocable-delegation principle, though the sources do not discuss ceremonial monarchy; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Liquid democracy is offered as a better form of democracy, so adherents back democracy; the worry about voters choosing badly is the one liquid advocates address through delegation to those who know better.

direct-votes.rationale: Voters can always vote directly on any issue and override a delegate, but the model also keeps delegation, so it is a hybrid rather than direct voting instead of representatives.

workers-councils.rationale: Liquid democracy rests on individual voters and flexible delegation across all citizens rather than council-based power; no source endorses councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Territorial questions are outside the model.

natural-rulers.rationale: The model rests on equal votes with trust conferred by voters and revocable at any time, rather than any class born fitter to rule; Valsangiacomo calls it anti-elitist.

political-violence-never.rationale: Its advocates pursue change through software and institutions, but the sources do not discuss violence; inferred from the procedural approach.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nothing in the model glorifies war; an inference from its deliberative, participatory orientation.

separate-church-state.rationale: The model does not address religion and the state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Authority in the model comes from voters and their delegates rather than any scripture; inferred, as the sources do not discuss religion.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Who supplies courts and defence is not a topic in liquid-democracy writing, which assumes public decisions made by voters.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence posture is a substantive foreign-policy matter the model leaves to voters; the sources are silent.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The model is silent on ethnic nationhood; Pirate-party users have generally been universalist but the sources do not say.

class-struggle-history.rationale: A theory of history is not part of the doctrine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The model equalises voting influence in principle, but takes no position on equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims are not addressed in the sources, and the model itself takes no side on them.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are a policy question the model does not address, and adherents have no shared view.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political union of civilizations is not covered by liquid-democracy writing, which is scale-neutral.

self-interest-moral.rationale: A claim in moral philosophy that the sources on liquid democracy never take up.

duties-before-rights.rationale: LiquidFeedback's founders speak of letting individuals keep their prerogatives, which fits individual rights first; inferred, not stated as a ranking.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics is not part of the doctrine, and the sources are silent.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is not addressed by the model or its sources.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The model embraces digital technology and industrial-era institutions are not its target; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Advocates favour technology for governance, but nothing says to speed change generally despite disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is a bioethical question outside the model, though tech-minded adherents may lean favourable.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Delegation in the model goes to named human proxies the voter chooses and can revoke, not to algorithms; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Founders discuss verifiability and fraud risks of e-voting and Pirate-party users value privacy, but the sources do not take a stand on encryption; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The model is an innovation, a reform of present institutions rather than restoration; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Advocates frame the model as a practical fix that lets people decide issue by issue, but it is not stated as an anti-ideological principle.

direct-action.rationale: The model is meant to work through votes and complement elections rather than replace them with direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Parties such as the Pirates use liquid democracy internally, practicing the participatory politics they advocate; not stated as a general principle in the sources.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The model is a digital-age institution and has no link to primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Topic-specific delegation relies on specialised trust, which presupposes people have different areas of expertise.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Principles of distribution are not addressed; the model concerns who decides, not what is decided.

production-for-use.rationale: An economic organising principle the model leaves open, as the sources do not mention production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxian economic claim the sources on liquid democracy do not discuss.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by one class over another conflicts with equal votes for all and revocable delegation.

collective-farming.rationale: Farm organisation is an economic policy question the model does not decide.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A theory of imperialism that the sources on liquid democracy do not touch.

taxation-theft.rationale: The model assumes collective decisions bind everyone and treats voters as setting public policy; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Limits on state power over individual conduct are not discussed in the sources, so adherents' views are not known.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The group-versus-individual rights debate is not addressed, although the model counts individual voters, so no position is stated.

conscription.rationale: Military service is a substantive policy the model leaves to voters; the sources do not discuss it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The model is built on voice: more ways to vote and to take back delegations, and nothing treats exit as a stronger check.

state-as-business.rationale: The model treats citizens as participants, not customers; inferred from its participatory aims.

positive-liberty.rationale: A theory of freedom the sources do not engage, so no view can be attributed.

media-academia-power.rationale: A claim about real power in society that the sources on liquid democracy do not address.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed by the model, and it rests on equal citizenship; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Valsangiacomo says liquid democracy lets citizens choose proxies across topics and puts parties on an equal footing with other groups; fixed family or trade-body representation is not the model.

total-state.rationale: The model distributes decision power among voters and revocable delegates, contrary to a state directing all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the reformist, institutional aims.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the model's civic orientation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Delegations are revocable at any time and conditional on trust, the opposite of binding personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labor contradicts the equal-citizen premise of the model.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: An epistemological thesis outside the model, with nothing in the sources about it.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral universalism is not addressed by the sources and adherents differ.

single-common-good.rationale: The model aggregates differing preferences issue by issue and lets groups compete on a level field, as Valsangiacomo describes, rather than discovering one common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A national-question statement unrelated to the model, which the sources do not discuss.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship rules for diasporas are not discussed in the sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy is not part of the doctrine and the sources are silent.

workplace-democracy.rationale: LiquidFeedback is designed for any organisation, and Bollier's summary says it democratises decisions in organisations; the sources do not endorse worker control of large companies specifically.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding design is a policy matter the voters decide, not a commitment of the model.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: The link between economic and political freedom is not discussed in liquid-democracy writing.

rule-by-example.rationale: Liquid democracy relies on votes and revocable delegation rather than the example of rulers; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed; the model is scale-neutral.

force-without-un.rationale: Authorisation for force abroad is a foreign-policy matter the sources never mention.

reason-over-faith.rationale: A philosophical claim the model does not address, though its design relies on informed deliberation; no position stated.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility is a policy outcome the model does not decide.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not addressed in the sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: Industrial-relations doctrine is not addressed by the model.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nothing in the model concerns cultural institutions; inferred from its evolutionary, institution-complementing character.

dominated-front.rationale: A geopolitical alignment the sources do not discuss.

workers-nation.rationale: A labor-internationalism question outside the model.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The model rests on equal votes for all citizens; no source addresses gender roles, so inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is an economic-religious matter the model does not take up.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equal participation of all voters is basic to the model, which conflicts with racial classification in law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist theory of the state, absent from the sources on liquid democracy.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production policy is left to voters; the sources say nothing about it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Integration policy is not addressed in the sources, so no stance is inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory, not part of the model, and at odds with its evidence-based, open-process aim; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Valsangiacomo argues liquid democracy supports strong proportionality, with voters' choices tracked by weighted proxies.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the model's procedural, non-missionary character.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: A sociological claim that the sources on liquid democracy do not address.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Wikipedia says liquid democracy arose from political disillusionment, and founders stress elected leaders ignoring the public, though corruption itself is not their claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Coercive eugenics conflicts with the model's equal-rights premise.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional-justice policy is not covered; accountability of representatives is a theme but not this question.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The proper scope of government is not set by the model, which only governs how its decisions are made.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial discrimination conflicts with equal citizenship; inferred as the sources do not address it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The model gives each person one vote of equal weight before delegation, so equal standing underlies it, though this is not stated as a moral doctrine.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism, which the sources do not touch.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A historical-political classification outside the model.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law policy is not addressed by the sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the model's liberal, participatory orientation.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religiously linked policy question the model leaves to voters.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: School religion policy is not discussed in the sources.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist state doctrine unrelated to the model.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Delegations rest on the voter's conditional trust and can be withdrawn at any time, which expresses consent in a continuous form.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade aims are not discussed by the model or its sources.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority conflicts with equal citizenship; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian ethic the sources do not state; a hybrid democratic model that binds dissenters by vote does not clearly endorse or reject it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: A social-evolutionary thesis that the sources do not address.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed directly; the model puts parties on a level footing but nothing says whether parties hostile to the order may be banned.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Revocable delegation limits any representative's arbitrary power over voters, which fits the republican idea; the sources do not use that vocabulary.

separated-powers.rationale: Institutional checks are not discussed in the sources, though the model itself disperses power among delegates; no stated position.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined party leading the people conflicts with the model's emphasis on citizens choosing and recalling their own proxies.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Distributive priorities are a policy matter the model leaves to voters.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy outside the model.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor-law restrictions are not addressed in the sources.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: A Malthusian claim the sources on liquid democracy do not discuss.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: An empirical social claim not covered by the sources, so no stance is attributed.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Liquid democracy chooses representatives by voluntary delegation, which is a selection model; Landemore-style sortition is a different proposal, so adherents are mostly against replacing elections by lot.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The model is meant to increase accountability; inferred, as the sources do not discuss emergencies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price regulation in emergencies is a policy choice left to voters.

party-controls-media.rationale: The founders treat transparency and open discussion as central, which is incompatible with party control of information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; inferred against the party-state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed in the sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Delegates in the model are unpaid volunteers with no fixed office, but the sources do not take a position on pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Valsangiacomo notes a trade-off between liquid proxies' independence and party discipline, and delegates there act on their own convictions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational integration is not covered, though Pirate-party adherents often favour it; the sources do not say.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the model's distrust of concentrated authority.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the model and not discussed.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority in the model derives from voters, not from clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A revolutionary-socialist line on war that the sources never mention.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The founders emphasise open discussion; inferred, as censorship is not discussed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The model has no fixed terms; delegates serve while they hold trust, so term limits are not the relevant check.

recall-officials.rationale: Revocability at any time is a defining feature; Wikipedia calls recall central and Valsangiacomo discusses instant recall as the voter's last resort.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is a foreign-policy matter the model does not decide.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: An extreme housing policy that the model does not address.

people-in-arms.rationale: Military organisation is not discussed in the sources.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: A cultural-moral claim unrelated to the model.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not addressed by the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: A populist claim about graduates that the sources do not make, even though the model grew from distrust of political elites.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not part of the doctrine and the sources are silent.

death-penalty.rationale: Criminal punishment is left to voters under the model; the sources do not discuss it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum content is a policy outcome the model does not decide.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: School science curriculum is not addressed in the sources.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Content regulation is not discussed in the sources, and Pirate-milieu users are divided.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not addressed by the sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language rights are not addressed by liquid-democracy writing.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemption law is not discussed in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A Millian social-liberty claim that the sources do not make.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt policy is not covered by the sources.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: An anti-colonial economic thesis not covered by the sources.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Adherents favour broadly participatory constitution-making, and some propose liquid mechanisms for it, but the sources do not state it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The model is about expanding political participation; inferred against suspending freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid duties are not discussed in the sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy is outside the model.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Liquid democracy has no head of state in its design; some adherents favour direct election, others dispersed delegation, so it is genuinely open.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary governance is not addressed, though the model could in principle be applied to it; no stance.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: A territorial-conflict policy the sources do not address.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The justification of property is not discussed in the sources.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate on Soviet history that the sources do not touch.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is left to voters; the sources do not discuss it.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrine is not addressed by the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International-law status of annexation is not addressed, so neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not discussed in the sources.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The model has no head of state in its design and the sources do not discuss the office.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Territorial integrity is not addressed by the model; adherents in different countries would differ.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Constitutional autonomy arrangements are outside the doctrine and the sources do not discuss them.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine or hereditary sanctity of a ruler contradicts authority resting on revocable voter delegation.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is a policy outcome, not part of the voting model.

character-from-environment.rationale: A question of human nature on which the sources say nothing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A ruler unbound by law is the opposite of the accountability that revocable delegation builds in.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not part of the doctrine.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The model aims at one flat network of equal voters and proxies instead of reserved power for the few; inferred, since the sources do not discuss classical constitutions.

leader-cult.rationale: Founders put issues rather than leaders at the centre of politics, and a leader cult contradicts that.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is outside the model.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrinal question the sources do not touch.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is a substantive policy the model leaves to voters.

refugee-return.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; the sources do not address refugee questions.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism is not addressed; inferred against it from the civic, open-participation orientation.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Penalising leaving a religion contradicts voluntary, revocable association that is central to the model; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the model's liberal participatory stance.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not discussed in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-national unification is outside the model.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority self-government is not addressed in the sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A question of minority strategy the sources do not address.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Philosophy of history is not part of the doctrine.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not addressed by the model.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; bailout policy is a substantive question left to voters.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liquid democracy emphasises majority input and revocable proxies, but the sources do not oppose judicial review and Valsangiacomo discusses minority and fragmentation risks, so only a mild lean.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Valsangiacomo says liquid democracy supports descriptive representation in principle, but quotas are not discussed; adherents differ.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic bloc economics is unrelated to the model.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade policy is not addressed by the model.

moral-incentives.rationale: Work incentives are not addressed in the sources.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The founders present the tool as a complement to representative democracy, working peacefully through institutions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equal votes and authority rooted in voluntary delegation oppose inherited rank; inferred from the equality premise rather than quoted.

history-own-civilization.rationale: History teaching is not addressed by the model.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule by one society over another without consent is contrary to authority resting on voters' delegation.

patriotic-education.rationale: Civic education content is not addressed by the sources.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Admissions and hiring policy is outside the model.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not part of liquid democracy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: An economic-theory question the sources do not touch.

delink-world-market.rationale: Development strategy is outside the model.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory the sources do not touch.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal participation is basic to the model, but private discrimination is a separate matter the sources do not discuss, so only a weak inference.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The founders stress protection of minorities from noisy majorities in design, but the sources do not discuss constitutional entrenchment.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The legal status of colonial treaties is not discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Choice of those who hold power by the people, revocable at any time, is the core principle, though the model goes beyond periodic elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Bollier's summary stresses majority preference as the signal and a design for protecting minorities from noise, not a veto over decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Continuous revocation is a peaceful form of removing those who lose trust; the sources do not discuss resistance to lawbreaking rulers explicitly.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The model blurs the parliament-citizen line by letting voters decide directly, so the question has no clean answer in the sources.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed in the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use policy is not discussed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The model treats each citizen as an equal voter, not a duty-bound privileged class; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Liquid democracy depends on citizens engaging, directly or through chosen proxies; Wikipedia notes few citizens staying active as a weakness.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim the sources do not address.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim the sources do not address.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim outside the model.

native-born-offices.rationale: The model is open to any member of a polity and says nothing of birth; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: An international-communist question not in the sources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development policy is not discussed in the sources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial revanchism is not addressed by the model.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal votes for all citizens are the model's basis, which does not fit leadership reserved to one descent group; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional preambles are not discussed in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: A historical-political judgement not addressed in the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical-interpretation question the model does not address.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is a decision for voters and not addressed in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: A social-policy matter the sources do not address.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: A social-policy and empirical matter the sources do not address.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liquid democracy is promoted as a general design usable by any organisation, though its sources are mostly Western; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Political authority in the model rests on voters and recallable delegates, not on a military guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Recognition of care work is not discussed in the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: A family-ethics claim unrelated to the model.

office-by-exam.rationale: Valsangiacomo says proxies are chosen by voters' trust, not by credentials, though topic-specific delegation lets expertise count in practice.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Investment screening is not addressed in the sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Family law is not part of the doctrine.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Removal at any time is central, but Valsangiacomo describes proxies as acting on their own convictions, not mandated, so only partially agreed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is a policy matter the model leaves to voters.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure is not addressed in the sources.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The model has no fixed parliament, and the sources do not discuss budget approval.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land ownership by foreigners is not addressed by the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination law is not covered by the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: A cultural-economic claim the sources do not make.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is outside the model.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Forcible control of another state's system contradicts authority from voters' consent; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Valsangiacomo warns of interest-group pressure and oligarchic risk, and Wikipedia notes wealthy actors might dominate delegations; the founders' critique of representative politics supports mild agreement.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign-funding rules are not discussed in the sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population and family policy is not addressed by the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment policy is left to voters; the sources are silent.

democratic-peace.rationale: An international-relations claim the sources on liquid democracy do not discuss.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The model binds participants to votes they lost, but the sources do not discuss a general duty to obey law.

non-intervention.rationale: International-law principle not discussed by the sources.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is outside the model.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy against a minority is unsupported and contradicts equal citizenship; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not discussed by the sources.

public-access-to-information.rationale: LiquidFeedback's founders stress open, verifiable processes, and Wikipedia says voters can see what happened to their delegated votes; a general right of access is inferred from that transparency.

local-production.rationale: Economic localism is not covered by the sources.

informal-organisation.rationale: Liquid democracy gives formal, tracked delegation and structured decision procedures to groups, not informal trust-based circles; Pirate parties used it in formal organisations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The relation of national to international law is not discussed in the sources.

religious-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred against it from equal participation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: A tributary-order claim wholly outside the model.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not addressed in the sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist property doctrine not addressed in the sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: A Cold War stance the sources do not address.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service-delivery design is left to voters; the sources do not address it.

religion-illusion.rationale: A claim about religion that the sources do not make.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: A historical-economic judgement the sources do not address.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A feminist-economic thesis the sources do not address.

socialized-care.rationale: Domestic labor organisation is not addressed in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is not addressed in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaty status is not discussed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small communal society is not part of the model, which has been used in large parties and municipalities, but also not opposed.

majority-settlement.rationale: Targeted settlement of a majority group in minority regions is not discussed; inferred mild disagreement from equal-treatment premises.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: A third-way economic claim the sources do not address.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Competing territorial claims are not discussed in the sources.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is a falsehood, and the model's own case for informed decisions depends on evidence; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Criminalising a group's private life conflicts with equal participation; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The model needs open competition among proxies and open discussion, and suppression would defeat it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the open-discussion emphasis.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Governing territories for another's benefit without their voters conflicts with authority resting on those governed.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-legal obligation unrelated to the model.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Armed removal of rulers on religious grounds is opposed by peaceful, voter-controlled authority; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Liquid democracy is a participatory model that lets citizens decide issues directly or delegate by topic, though its sources do not address workplaces and universities specifically.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: An academic social theory not addressed in the sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender-law policy is not discussed in the sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: A medical-ethics question left to voters; the sources are silent.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Wikipedia and sources describe a procedural idea that can be used from any position, but do not declare left-right outdated.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept the sources do not engage.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The claim attributes a group's values to its religion and contradicts equal citizenship; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from voters' delegations in the model, not from God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Secularism rules are not discussed in the sources.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment-law policy is not addressed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic-model choice is left to voters; the sources take no position.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Defence policy is not addressed by the sources.

rich-first.rationale: A development-strategy claim not addressed in the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed in the sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inherited office contradicts authority resting on voters' revocable trust.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Banking design is not addressed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Debt policy is not discussed by the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: The model rests on equal votes for all citizens, not a property test; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist thesis the sources do not address.

reification.rationale: A Marxist critical concept the sources do not engage.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The statement is about press ownership, and the sources on liquid democracy do not discuss media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Open, verifiable procedures fit publicly announced rules, though the sources do not discuss rule-of-law doctrine.

racial-franchise.rationale: Equal participation for every voter is basic: each citizen has one vote and may vote directly or delegate; Valsangiacomo links the model to descriptive representation, not to restriction.

online-participation.rationale: The model is realised through online platforms such as LiquidFeedback, and Wikipedia traces it to Berlin hacker culture; the founders call it a concrete instantiation of liquid democracy.

open-government-data.rationale: Founders insist on public, verifiable votes and tracking of proposals, and Wikipedia says voters can see what happened to delegated votes; publication of all government records is a natural extension.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the equal-citizenship basis.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a minority is opposed to equal standing; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Both deliberative bodies and liquid voting aim to widen participation, but the sources do not discuss sortition panels, and Landemore-style sortition is a rival model; adherents differ.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not addressed in the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Valsangiacomo and Wikipedia warn of power concentrating among the wealthy in delegation networks, but the claim here is about wealth in general, which the sources do not make.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Military personnel policy is not discussed in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from open participation.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Policing and prisons are not addressed in the sources.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational design is not discussed in the sources, though minority protection is a design concern for LiquidFeedback, so no firm position.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Poverty-relief methods are not discussed in the sources.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing the wage system is a revolutionary economic aim with no connection to a voting-procedure model, so it is left neutral.

vote-delegation.rationale: Topic-specific, revocable delegation is the defining mechanism of liquid democracy.

term-limits.rationale: Liquid democracy is a decision procedure whose revocable delegation already lets voters remove representatives at any time; the sources take no stance on fixed term caps.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The model prescribes how decisions are made, not which risks deserve priority; the sources say nothing on extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: A procedural idea with no stance on religious institutions; Pirate-party and civic users hold varied views.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The model concerns collective decision procedure, not private household authority, and the sources never address it.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should be able to delegate their vote on each policy area to someone they trust and withdraw that delegation at any time.
missingStatements.rationale: Topic-specific, revocable delegation is the defining mechanism of liquid democracy, and no current statement asks about delegating votes.

missingStatements.text: Votes on public decisions should be open and verifiable by anyone rather than secret.
missingStatements.rationale: LiquidFeedback's founders reject secret electronic ballots because verifiable open voting guards against fraud, a design choice most democratic theory disputes.
missingStatements.declined: Open, non-secret voting is a LiquidFeedback design choice specific to this one ideology; not worth a bank slot.

notes: Liquid democracy is mostly a procedural idea, so about two thirds of the answers are neutral, low-confidence ones; adherents who are Pirate-party members tend to be liberal on civil liberties, but no source states this. Valsangiacomo notes proxies act on their own convictions rather than as mandated delegates, which is why the recallable-delegates answer is only +1.
